scope: E Reproductive / Breast first-learning cognition, Source handoff, retrieval, local closure and progressive compression only
rule: Organize the 20 stable E Blocks and 212 stable KP identities for learning without changing medical meaning, filling Source/visual gaps, silently modernizing staging/treatment, duplicating external Primary owners, inferring official-question membership, or manufacturing learner progress.

classes.WHOLE_BLOCK_SOURCE: one compact coherent original-Lecture unit may be consumed continuously before local retrieval
classes.NATURAL_SOURCE_UNITS: a long, multi-center or multi-source Block uses a small number of genuine Source sub-units; each Source unit may support several Logic Groups
classes.INTEGRATION_PRIMARY: reserved for a Block that genuinely synthesizes already-formed owners rather than owning a new continuous Primary Source; no E Block currently requires this class

source_contact_contract.hard_rule: Logic Group count never determines Source-contact count. VISUAL_REQUIRED is a closure/evidence requirement, not automatically a separate device handoff.

units: reproductive axis, feedback and PRL/OT control (P427–434)
normal → proliferation → in-situ pathology + original figures

visual_contract.rule: When a decisive relation is spatial or morphology-dependent, first formation requires real Current original-Source visual contact. Text may orient or later test retrieval but cannot certify a never-seen visual relation.
open_source_debt: E9-LG02 remains VISUAL_SOURCE_GAP for processus-vaginalis / hydrocele spatial relations.
E11-LG02 remains VISUAL_SOURCE_GAP for abscess-location / incision geometry.
E14-LG02 has only PARTIAL_SOURCE_PAGES_AVAILABLE; closure requires confirmed contact with the relevant original surgical visual rather than assuming the partial page set is sufficient.
visual_contract.non_blocking_visual_gap_rule: A Block may continue through non-visual cognition when Source truth is sufficient, but the named visual-dependent LG relation must remain unclosed until its required Source visual is actually available and contacted.

negative_space: no complete obstetrics/gynecology clinical curriculum, infertility/PCOS/ectopic pregnancy/labor/postpartum-management expansion
no complete male reproductive clinical curriculum, prostate Primary, torsion/epididymitis/testicular-tumor expansion
no full breast-imaging/pathology-specialty curriculum or silent BI-RADS expansion
no silent replacement of Current Study FIGO/AJCC/treatment wording by modern external guidelines or regimens
no duplicate Primary for generic HPV/STI/infection, tumor-general, endocrine-common or urinary/prostate truth
no model-prior completion of E7 Source Gap or E9/E10/E11 visual Source gaps
no inferred official E System-question membership or Question→Knowledge mapping
no learner-state/mastery claim from repository construction

repair_return.control_or_time_failure: repair the smallest failed SR Logic Group and reconstruct the local feedback/time transition
repair_return.lineage_location_or_barrier_failure: repair the smallest failed pathology Logic Group; use original morphology when the distinction is visual
repair_return.evidence_or_treatment_failure: repair the smallest evidence/treatment LG while preserving Current Study version boundary
repair_return.visual_relation_missing: return to the original Source visual; if the visual is currently unavailable, keep that relation unclosed rather than substituting prose
repair_return.precision_or_version_conflict: use Current Source context / Precision handling; do not modernize by model prior
repair_return.external_owner_missing: use the smallest-sufficient true external owner or Chat repair; do not create a second E Primary
repair_return.return_rule: after repair, return to the interrupted E mainline; repair evidence does not erase the original observation and does not prove mastery

SR1: D6 endocrine-common language when already learned
E2: generic HPV/infection owner and tumor-general invasion language when needed

system_route.external_missing_rule: If an external baseline has not actually been learned, use the smallest-sufficient repair for the current E action; do not manufacture learner completion or a new hard repository dependency.
system_route.hard_edge_rule: Delete the edge. If the later Block can still form from its own accepted Primary Source with bounded local reactivation and without hidden guessing or duplicate first teaching, the edge is not hard.
system_route.flex_rule: Hard legality is intentionally sparse. SR1–SR6, E1–E13 remain enterable from their own accepted Primary Source even when earlier E Blocks are strongly beneficial. E13→E14 is the sole inside-E hard edge because E14 intentionally consumes accepted T/N/M and receptor-state outputs rather than re-owning them. The default route remains low-switching guidance only.

first_pass_chain: System orientation in KianOS around the accepted two-trunk E model
bounded Block / natural Source-unit orientation and stop-line
continuous original Lecture contact in iPad/MarginNote for genuine new Source content and decisive original visuals
one normal return after the relevant natural Source contact rather than one return per Logic Group
active KP retrieval by accepted Logic-Group learner order
cognition-specific Logic-Group closure; visual-required LGs require actual visual evidence and fail closed when the Source visual is missing
after all Block LGs close: Block Recall
optional non-gating Partial-System Reconstruction at five natural compression points
after all 20 Blocks are actually learned: final E System Reconstruction
later trusted official E System-question sweep only after exact E question membership Source boundary closes

partial_system_reconstructions.target: controller → gonadal cell/output → cycle phase → fertilization signal → hCG/corpus-luteum/placental relay
partial_system_reconstructions.closure: solve a novel hormone/time problem by control layer + target cell + phase + feedback without replaying Block titles

partial_system_reconstructions.target: normal compartment → location/type/growth change → atypia → barrier breach, while degeneration remains a separate operation
partial_system_reconstructions.closure: classify a uterine/cervical lesion by operation and barrier state before disease label

partial_system_reconstructions.target: villus/lineage → morphology/genetics/marker → local invasion → independently assess metastatic competence / spread
partial_system_reconstructions.closure: separate lineage, invasion and dissemination in a new trophoblastic/ovarian prompt

partial_system_reconstructions.target: normal duct-lobule-myoepithelium → production/ejection/drainage → benign/cyclic/duct symptom vs stasis/infection/source control vs malignant alarm
partial_system_reconstructions.closure: localize a breast symptom to function/compartment and keep infection vs malignancy discrimination open until evidence resolves it

partial_system_reconstructions.target: lineage/normal unit → in-situ vs invasion → local/regional/distant extent → receptor evidence → local/regional/systemic/targeted control
partial_system_reconstructions.closure: derive a breast-cancer decision path from identity and extent rather than reciting TNM/subtype/treatment tables

SR1.goal: controller → pituitary relay → gonadal effector/cell target
SR1.closure: place GnRH, FSH/LH and male/female target cells on the correct control layer before predicting an effect

SR1.goal: terminal-hormone feedback, inhibin selectivity and the preovulatory positive-feedback exception
SR1.closure: given a change in sex steroid or inhibin, identify the feedback direction and the upstream variable affected

SR1.goal: PRL production vs OT ejection and endocrine-axis vs direct/neuroendocrine control
SR1.closure: separate production, ejection, source and control mode without flattening PRL and OT into one lactation hormone
solve an unfamiliar reproductive-hormone prompt by source layer → target cell → feedback/reflex → changed variable → physiologic phase

SR2.goal: testicular spaces, Sertoli/germ/Leydig roles and blood-testis barrier
SR2.closure: localize a male-reproductive function or failure to compartment and cell before naming a hormone

SR2.goal: FSH-Sertoli and LH-Leydig parallel chains with ABP/inhibin/testosterone outputs
SR2.closure: rebuild the two gonadotropin chains and predict which output changes when one branch fails

SR2.goal: androgen action, feedback, metabolism and testosterone↔DHT/local conversion boundaries
SR2.closure: distinguish systemic androgen output, local conversion and feedback without importing prostate Primary
put the three sperm-competence stages in order and state what each newly enables
route a prostate, liver, lipid or fertility extension to the correct owner instead of expanding SR2

SR3.goal: E/P effects across endometrium, myometrium, cervix, tube, vagina, breast and systemic interfaces
SR3.closure: predict the direction of an E/P effect at a named target tissue without using a flat hormone-effects list

SR3.goal: withdrawal → recruitment → dominant follicle → high-E positive feedback/LH surge → ovulation → luteal progesterone
SR3.closure: reconstruct the causal cycle from hormone withdrawal through luteal state and identify the first broken transition

SR3.goal: ovarian, endometrial and hormone axes plus basal-temperature marker
SR3.closure: align the three time axes and explain why basal temperature marks a phase without causing ovulation

SR3.goal: organ-operation boundary and closed-book cycle reconstruction
SR3.closure: use organ role + time phase to rebuild a cycle question without replaying KP labels

SR4.goal: steroid precursor flow and two-cell/two-gonadotropin ovarian synthesis
SR4.closure: from the original two-cell Source figure, trace substrate/cell/hormone movement and explain why granulosa cells depend on theca input

SR4.goal: male/female gonadal mirror plus luteal, placental and postmenopausal source shifts
SR4.closure: given sex or life stage, name the dominant source/cell and explain what changed from the previous stage

SR4.goal: source-target interface to breast endocrine treatment
SR4.closure: state the estrogen-source logic relevant to therapy without importing E14 treatment details

SR5.goal: fertilization competence and the cycle-end fork: withdrawal vs rescue
SR5.closure: connect successful fertilization to the decision that prevents ordinary luteal withdrawal

SR5.goal: hCG source/identity/time → pregnancy corpus-luteum rescue → placental takeover
SR5.closure: rebuild the early-pregnancy endocrine relay and identify which source owns steroid support at each phase

SR5.goal: placental hormone roles, fetal-placental E3 interface, progesterone uterine quiescence and bounded labor interface
SR5.closure: separate placental outputs by role and keep Study-bounded labor claims distinct from full obstetric management
reconstruct fertilization signal → hCG → corpus luteum → placenta → late-pregnancy hormonal state from memory

SR6.goal: duct-lobule/alveolus-myoepithelial unit and E/P developmental roles
SR6.closure: locate duct, secretory unit and myoepithelium and assign E/P developmental effects correctly

SR6.goal: PRL production vs OT ejection under sucking reflex
SR6.closure: trace sucking through both control chains and predict which observable fails when PRL or OT is missing

SR6.goal: production vs ejection vs drainage plus hPL/PRL/OT and myoepithelial role
SR6.closure: localize a lactation failure to production, ejection or drainage before naming a hormone or lesion

SR6.goal: stasis/infection entry plus compression of reproductive physiology into breast physiology
SR6.closure: explain how normal flow failure creates the E11 entry while preserving the control/time trunk

E1.goal: normal epithelial geography → ectopy → squamous metaplasia
E1.closure: given a red cervical surface or epithelial change, distinguish location change from cell-type change and true tissue loss

E1.goal: chronic-cervicitis manifestations, polyp and Nabothian retention cyst mechanisms
E1.closure: map red/protruding/cystic findings to inflammation, proliferation or gland-outlet obstruction

E1.goal: reverse localization from appearance to structural operation
E1.closure: classify an unfamiliar cervical appearance by location/type/defect/retention before considering neoplasia

E2.goal: koilocytosis/atypia distribution, SIL depth and basement-membrane boundary
E2.closure: using Current pathology Source, distinguish LSIL, HSIL and gland involvement without mistaking gland entry for stromal invasion

E2.goal: high-risk HPV E6/E7 → p53/RB and p16 as supporting marker
E2.closure: rebuild cause vs marker roles and avoid treating p16 as the causal event

E2.goal: cervical cancer identity, in-situ/microinvasive/invasive boundary and Current Study extent language
E2.closure: separate epithelial identity, basement-membrane breach, local extent and route of spread without silently modernizing staging

E2.goal: layer → basement membrane → molecular driver → extent
E2.closure: solve a new cervical-pathology prompt in that order

E3.goal: endometriosis vs adenomyosis and cyclic bleeding consequences
E3.closure: use location + retained cyclic response to distinguish ectopic endometrium, myometrial involvement and ovarian chocolate cyst
separate physiologic proliferation, hyperplasia/atypia and carcinoma by growth state and invasion
classify an unfamiliar endometrial/myometrial lesion without collapsing ectopy, hyperplasia and invasion

E4.goal: myometrial origin, benign identity and fascicular/whorled morphology
E4.closure: recognize leiomyoma from tissue, border and morphology rather than from the word 'mass'

E4.goal: hyaline vs red degeneration and pregnancy/thrombosis context
E4.closure: explain a degenerative change without converting degeneration/necrosis into automatic malignancy
prioritize malignant cellular evidence over degeneration when separating leiomyoma from leiomyosarcoma

E5.goal: trophoblastic-disease map, normal villus layers and hydropic villus morphology
E5.closure: identify the villous/trophoblastic structure present before reasoning about genetics or malignancy

E5.goal: complete vs partial mole by villus involvement, fetal tissue, parental origin and p57
E5.closure: derive complete/partial identity from structure → fetus → parental contribution → p57 rather than memorizing isolated signs
solve a molar-pregnancy identification prompt using the four-step sequence

E6.goal: villus presence, trophoblast identity and invasive-mole local invasion separated from metastatic competence
E6.closure: distinguish myometrial/vessel invasion from true distant metastatic growth; use invasive mole as the explicit counterexample

E6.goal: choriocarcinoma structure, hematogenous spread, clinical reverse clues and bounded treatment direction
E6.closure: identify choriocarcinoma by absent villi + hemorrhagic behavior + true hematogenous spread without importing full clinical regimens

E6.goal: PSTT hPL/intermediate-trophoblast identity plus final villus-cell-invasion-spread-hormone algorithm
E6.closure: route an unfamiliar trophoblastic tumor by villus → cell → invasion → spread → hormone

E7.goal: ovarian lineage map and stromal-invasion cancer threshold
E7.closure: name the lineage first and keep papillary architecture separate from true invasion

E7.goal: serous vs mucinous four-axis comparison plus psammoma support
E7.closure: classify epithelial ovarian morphology from laterality/cystic content/papillae/psammoma and then independently judge invasion

E7.goal: primary mucinous tumor vs Krukenberg plus reverse algorithm
E7.closure: use laterality + GI-source evidence to separate primary ovarian disease from metastatic ownership

E8.goal: germ-cell lineage and teratoma maturity as the malignancy axis
E8.closure: judge teratoma behavior from tissue maturity rather than number of germ layers

E8.goal: yolk-sac tumor identity, AFP and Schiller-Duval morphology
E8.closure: contact the decisive Current Source morphology and combine structure + AFP without using AFP alone as diagnosis

E8.goal: granulosa vs thecoma by malignancy tendency, hormone direction and morphology
E8.closure: identify the sex-cord/stromal tumor from cell morphology and estrogenic output

E8.goal: source lineage → maturity → marker → structure → hormone
E8.closure: solve an ovarian non-epithelial tumor prompt with the five-step sequence

E9.goal: cryptorchid position, age/timing and special branches
E9.closure: treat cryptorchidism first as incomplete descent and route timing/exception questions without importing a full male clinic

E9.goal: processus-vaginalis patency and hydrocele compartment/communication types
E9.closure: distinguish fluid compartments and communication state; visual closure remains fail-closed until the missing original Source visual is recovered
classify by testis palpability + fluid/air content + positional change while preserving hernia ownership outside E

E10.goal: localized benign-mass coordinate and fibroadenoma recognition/handling
E10.closure: recognize a mobile circumscribed young-woman mass and keep pathology confirmation separate from malignant alarm

E10.goal: fibrocystic/cystic hyperplasia as a cycle-linked tissue response and bounded management
E10.closure: use cyclicity as the strongest discriminator and avoid expanding into a complete imaging algorithm

E10.goal: intraductal papilloma and nipple-discharge color as weighted evidence
E10.closure: treat discharge color as evidence weight, not a diagnosis, and identify when a duct lesion is the leading model

E10.goal: plasma-cell mastitis, nipple inversion and benign/inflammatory/malignant reverse sorting
E10.closure: route inflammatory or nipple findings by mechanism while keeping malignancy as a live alternative when warranted

E11.goal: drainage failure → stasis → bacterial entry/inflammation plus emptying/antimicrobial Study rules
E11.closure: localize the first failed drainage step and explain why restoring flow and controlling infection are distinct actions

E11.goal: mastitis→abscess transition and anatomy-directed drainage/source control
E11.closure: choose a drainage concept from abscess location and cavity structure; visual closure remains fail-closed until the missing original surgical visual is recovered

E11.goal: acute mastitis vs inflammatory breast cancer plus reverse source-control algorithm
E11.closure: separate infection evidence from malignant inflammatory presentation before committing to an infection-only model

E12.goal: normal duct/lobule-myoepithelium reference → usual vs atypical proliferation + risk context
E12.closure: anchor pathology in normal compartment identity and distinguish risk/background from actual malignant identity

E12.goal: classification responsibilities plus in-situ disease, DCIS/comedo and LCIS
E12.closure: from Current pathology Source, keep malignant epithelial identity separate from preserved myoepithelial/basement-membrane boundary

E12.goal: invasive NST/lobular and selected special morphologies
E12.closure: recognize invasion and lineage-specific morphology without collapsing all invasive cancers into one generic tumor pattern

E12.goal: inflammatory cancer, skin signs, lymphatic and hematogenous spread
E12.closure: derive dimple vs peau d'orange from the affected structure and keep local invasion, nodal spread and distant spread distinct

E12.goal: origin → barrier → morphology → spread → receptor interface
E12.closure: reconstruct the breast-cancer pathology model without reciting subtype lists

E13.goal: diagnostic contract and T coordinate including T0/Tis/T1–3/T4
E13.closure: separate identity from local extent and recognize T4 as structure/skin/chest-wall involvement rather than size alone

E13.goal: N coordinate, Current Study stage combinations and M0/M1
E13.closure: assemble Current Study stage from T/N/M while preserving version boundary instead of importing modern AJCC

E13.goal: ER/PR, HER2, Ki-67 and Current Study molecular-subtype logic
E13.closure: separate prognostic/predictive evidence dimensions and identify the treatment-relevant receptor pattern
use symptom/sign location to decide what it suggests without letting one sign replace tissue diagnosis

E13.goal: screening imaging, histologic gold standard and bounded supplemental/genetic/marker evidence
E13.closure: order evidence by role: detect → establish tissue identity → characterize extent/biology, without building a full imaging specialty

E13.goal: confirm identity → define extent → define molecular state
E13.closure: solve a new breast-cancer workup prompt in that sequence

E14.goal: local/regional/systemic/targeted objectives and modified-radical surgery variants
E14.closure: state the treatment objective before selecting a named operation and distinguish what the operation changes anatomically

E14.goal: axillary levels, extended/total mastectomy and breast-conserving local-control choices
E14.closure: use the relevant original/partial surgical Source to map local/axillary anatomy to operation choice; if the decisive visual is absent, do not claim visual mastery

E14.goal: clinical axillary status and sentinel-node branching
E14.closure: choose sentinel vs dissection logic from nodal evidence without treating the branch as a generic surgery rule

E14.goal: Current Study chemotherapy indications and bounded subtype rule
E14.closure: separate nodal/high-risk/systemic-clone indications from local surgery and preserve Study-specific chemotherapy wording
state why local residual-risk control is required after conservation
map receptor evidence to treatment class while keeping regimen details outside Current Source
build a treatment plan from objective layers rather than reciting operation/drug names

compression.ladder: 212 KP → 78 LG → 20 Block Recall → 5 non-gating PSR → final E System Reconstruction
compression.block_recall_rule: rebuild the governing medical problem; do not recite KP labels

final_system_reconstruction.target: two coupled trunks: reproductive control/time + tissue/compartment identity; independently track location/type/growth, barrier invasion, metastatic competence/spread, evidence/receptor and treatment objective; use transport/drainage only where it is a real mechanism
forbidden: treat the default route as ontology or all benefits_from relations as hard prerequisites
collapse local invasion into metastatic competence
claim E9/E11 visual mastery from prose-only Source gaps
import missing full gynecology, male-reproductive or breast-specialty curricula

compression.second_pass: decisive time/feedback transitions + lineage/location/barrier discriminations + real morphology/visual relations + stage/receptor/treatment objectives + Source/version boundaries + Wrong/Uncertain evidence; do not replay all 78 LGs by default
compression.late_review: two-trunk mother model + five PSR skeletons + invasion-vs-spread distinction + decisive visual morphologies + Current Study version boundaries + real personal weak points

A3 / urinary owner: prostate/urinary Primary remains outside E

cross_system_handoff.fine_grain_rule: System-level interfaces are allowed; finer external Block/KP routing fails closed without separately reviewed Current authority.

requirements_if_later_eligible: support explicit Logic-Group membership and the single E13→E14 hard readiness edge
support mixed Source-contact units without per-LG device bouncing
carry VISUAL_REQUIRED and visual-source-gap states as closure evidence without fabricating visual contact
preserve Current Study staging/treatment version boundaries
preserve external-primary Lecture ownership and fail-closed official-question membership
projection_boundary.rule: Projection may not rewrite E Learning Logic to fit a contiguous-range loader or existing page schema.

builder_self_checks: 20/20 Blocks and 212/212 KP identities covered exactly once by 78 LGs.
Default route is non-hard; only E13→E14 survives the builder delete-edge test as inside-E hard readiness.
Eight Blocks use NATURAL_SOURCE_UNITS and twelve use WHOLE_BLOCK_SOURCE; Logic Group count does not set handoff count.
Visual-dependent relations preserve E9/E11 missing-visual debt and E14 partial-visual uncertainty instead of manufacturing closure.
Five PSRs are non-gating compression opportunities, not new hierarchy or learner debt.
